messages:
nina: Heads-up from morningincident: several tenants on dedicated pools started getting 429s even though their prewarm credits should have been available. suspected cause: operator failover wiped transient ledger. quick sync?

leo: saw traces. admission path short-circuits to operator-local tokens, and when the operator restarted it re-registered the pool with zero ephemeral tokens. control-plane had the reservations but not the running counters.

priya: is this the same class we discussed where we trade a local fast-path for weaker recovery semantics?

omar: yes. tradeoff historically was avoiding an RPC on the hot path. but this outage shows the recovery gap is too large.

nina: thought experiment: what if autoscaler and admission both used the same durable lease+ledger snapshot so a restarted operator could reconstruct counters from lease logs?

leo: idea: compacted reservation deltas stored per-pool for the last N minutes. on restart operator asks control-plane for the delta stream and replays to rebuild ephemeral tokens. pretty similar to WAL-replay but scoped to pool and short retention.

priya: retention window question. if a pool has low churn, N can be small. for bursty tenants we need longer. maybe adaptive retention: size based on observed burst frequency per-tenant.

omar: adaptive retention adds complexity but reduces storage. also need to bound replay latency: we don't want operators stuck replaying 10s of MB before serving. cap replay to e.g. 2s of replay work then fallback to central admit RPC.

nina: fallback path is key. if rebuild times out, operator should transparently switch to central atomic admit RPC for safety. that keeps correctness at cost of latency.

leo: implement signals: operator_rebuild_count, rebuild_duration_seconds, fallback_admit_rate. alert if fallback_admit_rate > 5% over 5m for a pool.

priya: interface: control-plane needs new endpoints: RequestDeltaStream(pool_id, since_seq) and CommitEpoch(pool_id, operator_id, epoch, last_seq). CommitEpoch returns rebuilt_balance or a NEEDS_CENTRAL flag. idempotent semantics.

omar: also add a pool-lease row: owner_operator, lease_expiry. registration fails if another owner holds a non-expired lease. helps prevent split-brain.

nina: how does this interact with autoscaler pre-warm? Autoscaler creates reservations ahead of time; those deltas must be included in the compacted stream. otherwise rebuilt balance misses prewarm reserves.

leo: autoscaler should write prewarm intents into the same reservation log (compacted). keep intent vs allocated flags so replay knows which are usable tokens.

priya: operation plan: 1) add compacted per-pool delta table and small migration to provision it, 2) implement RequestDeltaStream and CommitEpoch, 3) operator replay + timeout + central fallback, 4) metrics + alerts, 5) rollout in canary (1 region) then 10% pools.

omar: migration note: delta table adds modest bytes per-reservation. we can GC based on per-pool retention policy. need a migration script and zero-downtime backfill (just start writing deltas, no backfill needed).

nina: fallback performance: central admit RPC must be very cheap. recommend a single-key Redis atomic INCR with lua guard to make it <1ms p50. but that adds a dependency and ops surface.

leo: or use a lease-style token bucket in control-plane with optimistic local fast-path and Redis as the ground truth. both are fine; pick Redis for speed.

priya: runbook change: on operator upgrade or restart, operators should try graceful handoff: acquire new epoch, snapshot delta cursor, then restart. we still tolerate uncoordinated restarts via replay+fallback.

omar: monitoring: instrument prewarm-success-rate and tail 99 admission latency when fallback used. low-latency tenants care about this.

nina: who wants what: Leo -> proto for delta stream API + Redis admit prototype; Priya -> retention policy heuristics and alert thresholds; Omar -> runbook + migration script and GC plan. I'll draft the RFC follow-up with sequence diagrams.

devops-bot: Created INC-2026-0424 for follow-up actions. Auto-tag: operator_failover.
